answer: Sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted peer attestation. Before an agent may endorse others it must lock a bond, and its influence grows only as independent peers confirm real work over time. A sybil farm must then post genuine collateral for every fake identity while earning nothing, since attestations from new, unendorsed agents are discounted. Reaching the summit of influence demands many distinct, bonded, mutually verified agents, turning a cheap flood of identities into a costly, slow campaign. Newcomers begin instead in a small oasis of limited trust, a probationary violet tier.
